preamble.summary:
This plan takes phax and @lbdremy/phax-schemas from Effect 3 to a green Effect 4 tree in one run and one pull request. It installs effect 4.1.2, applies the codemod, then migrates the topics in the spec's order: schema first, then errors, services and core, then the package and its JSON Schemas, then guidance and docs. It builds on the two groundwork plans merged in #195 and #196, described in CONTRIBUTING.md under "The Effect 4 migration": the behaviour corpus and its replay, the codemod with its rules and type-error ratchet, the test ratchet, the skills `.claude/skills/effect4-*`, the refusal model `src/schemas/refusal/`, and `docs/effect-4-mapping.md`. It is not the spec's last plan. The last plan removes the codemod, the vendored reference, the migration skills, the `effect-migration` profile and the protected paths, after the operator lifts them.

Why one run. CI runs `pnpm check:full` on every pull request, and no tree between the install and the last topic passes it. So the run goes from Effect 3 to green Effect 4 on one branch (`phax/effect-4-migration`).

What the operator does around the run (none of it is a phase's work):

1. Before the run, move `effect-migration` to be the first entry of `gateProfiles` in `phax.json`. `phax run` gates with the first profile listed. Put `standard` back first at the merge (operator decision, 2026-11-09). On every phase, `effect-migration` runs `pnpm format`, `pnpm codemod:effect4 --ratchet` (the type-error and test ratchets) and `pnpm lint`. On the terminal phase it adds `pnpm check:full`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm site:build`, `pnpm deno:smoke` and `pnpm deno:smoke-binary`.
2. Answer q-commit-counts before approval. With the recommended option, also fill the numbers into phase-01's commit body.
3. Start the run with `phax run --allow-skill-edits`. phase-09 edits three skill files: `.claude/skills/state-machines/SKILL.md`, `.claude/skills/infrastructure-adapters/SKILL.md` and `.claude/skills/observability/SKILL.md`.

Protected and read-only paths. `phax.json` declares `protectedPaths`: today the corpus baseline, `tests/effect4Corpus/corpus.ts`, `scripts/effect4-codemod/counts.ts`, both tsconfigs and `vitest.config.ts`. Declaring them also protects `phax.json` itself. Every phase also treats these as read-only:
- the paths CONTRIBUTING.md and spec §10 name: the corpus cases `tests/effect4Corpus/cases/**`, the corpus tests `tests/unit/effect4Corpus/**`, and the codemod's `main.ts`, `ratchet.ts` and `passingTests.ts`;
- the released JSON Schema snapshots `packages/schemas/snapshots/**`, the CLI contract fixtures, and every test that holds no Effect code.

A test that uses Effect is edited for its Effect plumbing only. No expected text, JSON, exit code, decoded value or refusal line moves (§5.14). No phase changes `package.json`'s `scripts`: the ratchet fails when they differ from HEAD's.

Rules every phase follows:
- Each phase's first instruction names the one skill it follows, or the codemod (§5.10). Every symbol is resolved through `effect4-lookup`: the vendored reference `docs/vendor/effect-migration/effect@4.1.2/`, then its topic guide, then the installed `node_modules/effect` source. Never training data, never the network.
- No compatibility module, in src or in tests, even for one phase. No `any`. No `as` that stands in for a type the migration broke; `as const` and fixture brand casts are allowed. No invented API (§5.11).
- No persisted format bump. No `next` snapshot, no stamp move, no new frozen decoder (§5.18).
- A failure found late that belongs to an earlier topic is fixed in the phase that finds it, at that symbol only and by the owning topic's skill, and named in the handoff.

Commands. Phases run the codemod as `pnpm exec tsx scripts/effect4-codemod/main.ts`, with `--check` for the report alone; this is the same script as `pnpm codemod:effect4`. They read type errors with `node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit`, adding `-p tsconfig.test.json` for the test suite. They run chosen tests with `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run <files>`. If an entry path differs in the installed version, take it from that package's `bin` field. `pnpm codemod:effect4 --ratchet`, `pnpm format`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm check:full`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm site:build` and the two Deno smokes are gate commands, so every phase may run them too.
preamble.requiredCommandsNote:
All three are already in `security.agentCommands` in phax.json, so the plan needs no PHAX security configuration change and grants no new command:
- `pnpm add` installs effect 4.1.2 in phase-01, the way the first groundwork plan installed ts-morph.
- `pnpm exec tsx` runs the codemod, the schemas scripts and the one-off capture and re-pin scripts.
- `node` runs tsc and vitest from node_modules, plus small file-copy and digest scripts.

`pnpm add` needs the npm registry. If the phase-01 session cannot reach it, the phase stops before the codemod and says so. It does not vendor the package or hand-edit the lockfile. The operator then installs in the phase worktree from outside the session (see phase-01).
technicalArbitrations:
Phase cut. The schema topic is split in two:
- phase-02 migrates the current schemas, the refusal adapter, `tests/effect4Corpus/subjects.ts` and the schema call sites in src, tests, scripts and site;
- phase-04 migrates the 63 frozen decoders, and only they.
The JSON Schema generator and the package move to phase-08. The errors, services and core topics take one phase each.
Order: errors (phase-05), then services (phase-06), then core (phase-07). Errors goes first because its blockers (`Either.flatMap`, `Either.flip`, `Either.Left`, `Either.getOrNull`, …) hold back 452 covered uses that a codemod re-run then rewrites mechanically. It is also the largest remaining error source, so after it the most tests load and the later phases get real test evidence. Services follows because the ports were already rewritten by the codemod's context-tag rule and one leftover remains; its risk is layer and runtime wiring, which the app tests exercise once errors are done. Core comes last as the sweep of whatever no other topic owns.
Loss accepted: phase-02 sets a pattern on about 400 schema uses and phase-04 repeats it on the decoders, so a wrong idiom costs two phases to unwind, mitigated by the review stop at phase-03. Each topic is one large diff rather than several small ones.

The Effect 4 generator diff is measured in phase-08, not phase-01. In phase-01 no phax schema module loads on Effect 4: the codemod changes no source by hand, and `src/schemas/publishedJsonSchema.ts` and `packages/schemas/build/jsonSchemas.ts` still use JSONSchema and SchemaAST, which Effect 4 removed. So the first tree that can render on Effect 4 is phase-08's.
phase-08 records, per format, what Effect 4 renders differently from the latest released snapshot (parsed, annotations aside) as a new section of `docs/effect-4-mapping.md`. It also builds the ajv equivalence judge in `packages/schemas/build/equivalence.ts` and wires it into `checkSnapshots` and `scripts/schemas-check.ts`.
Loss accepted: if Effect 4's generator cannot express a format at all, the run learns it only at phase-08, after the topic phases are spent.

The package ships a frozen copy of its JSON Schemas. In phase-01, before the install, the base's Effect 3 rendering of `packages/schemas/json/` is captured into `packages/schemas/shipped-json.json` (file name to exact content). From phase-08 on, the build writes `json/` from that file for every format without a `next` snapshot, and renders from the generator only for a format that has one. `scripts/schemas-check.ts --write` refreshes an entry when it records a `next`.
This is the only way to keep the shipped files byte-identical (§5.19). Shipping the latest released snapshots instead cannot work: `record-manifest.schema.json` has no snapshot, and a snapshot can lag its shipped file in annotations, because snapshots ignore annotations.
Loss accepted: a committed generated artifact beside the snapshots, which the build ships verbatim.

The history lock is refreshed in two commits, each naming the Effect 4 migration:
- phase-01: the codemod rewrites `src/schemas/history/` mechanically, since it targets all of src;
- phase-04: the hand migration of the decoders.
phase-04 migrates every v3 symbol under `src/schemas/history/`, of every topic, which the effect4-schema skill allows for that path. Later codemod re-runs then find nothing there, and no third refresh happens. The codemod is deterministic per file, so phase-02 and phase-03 leave history bytes untouched.
Loss accepted: the brief's single refresh becomes two. Avoiding that would mean restoring the codemod's history rewrites in phase-01, which needs a git command the sessions are not granted.

One review stop: phase-03, an interactive phase right after phase-02. The corpus replays the words, but nothing mechanical checks the Effect 4 idiom phase-02 chooses, or the absence of silencing `as` and `any` (ac-no-silencing is a diff search, not a gate). phase-04 repeats that idiom on 63 frozen decoders and phase-08 repeats it on the package and generator. No other stop is declared; the operator can hold any phase with `phax run --hold`.
Loss accepted: the run stops once and waits for a person.

No acceptance phase, although an acceptance provider is configured. The acceptance tests of this migration already exist and are frozen: the behaviour corpus, its replay and package tests, and the protected test contract, all written before any source moved. The test ratchet also refuses a recorded test file that adds `.fails` markers.
Loss accepted: the new checks of phase-08 (equivalence judge, shipped-JSON identity, Effect 4 exports) are written with their code, in-phase, not frozen beforehand.

The last code phase, phase-08, runs `pnpm check:full`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm site:build` and both Deno smokes itself, and leaves them green. phase-09 then starts from a green tree and only risks doc failures at the terminal gate.
Loss accepted: the full gate runs twice at the end, and phase-08 may have to fix a late failure owned by an earlier topic (see the preamble rule).

openQuestions.question: phax writes a phase's commit body verbatim from the plan, so phase-01's body cannot pick up numbers the codemod prints during the run. How does phase-01's commit carry the four type-error counts and each rule's rewrite count (§5.7)?

options.label: Before approving, the operator installs effect 4.1.2 and runs `pnpm codemod:effect4` on a scratch checkout of the run's base. They write the printed numbers over the placeholders in phase-01's commit body. phase-01 checks its own printed numbers against the body and stops on any difference
options.abandons: Approval waits on a manual dry run, and the numbers hold only for that base: any merge to main before the run starts means re-measuring, editing the body and re-approving

options.label: phase-01 commits with the placeholders and records the real numbers in docs/effect-4-mapping.md. The operator rewords phase-01's commit body with those numbers before the pull request merges
options.abandons: The run branch's history as phax recorded it: rewording phase-01 rewrites every later phase's commit, so the hashes the run's records and the reviewed pull request point at no longer exist

openQuestions.rationale: The codemod is deterministic and the base is fixed, so a scratch run gives exactly the numbers phase-01 will print, and phase-01's own check catches any drift. Rewording rewrites nine phases' commits after phax has recorded them. If reword is chosen, phase-01's instruction to compare its numbers with the body is dropped; phase-01 still writes them into docs/effect-4-mapping.md.

phases.title: Install effect 4.1.2 and apply the codemod
phases.objective: phax and @lbdremy/phax-schemas depend on effect 4.1.2 and on no other Effect package. The codemod has applied every mechanical rewrite, and the ratchet holds the first type-error counts and the first set of passing tests that later phases are measured against. The Effect 3 rendering of the shipped JSON Schemas is captured beforehand, as the byte reference for phase-08.
detailedInstructions: Follows: the codemod (scripts/effect4-codemod). This phase changes no source file by hand. Every change to a `.ts` file comes from the codemod or `pnpm format`.

Step 1, before installing anything, on Effect 3: capture the shipped JSON Schemas.
- Run `pnpm exec tsx scripts/schemas-json.ts`. It writes `packages/schemas/json/`, which is gitignored.
- With a small node script, write `packages/schemas/shipped-json.json`: a JSON object from each file name in `packages/schemas/json/` to that file's exact content as a string. Keys sorted, rendered as `JSON.stringify(value, null, 2)` plus a trailing newline.
- Check that every entry equals its file byte for byte.
- Add `packages/schemas/shipped-json.json` to `ignorePatterns` in `.oxfmtrc.json`, so `pnpm format` never touches it.

Step 2: remove the platform packages by hand.
- In `package.json`, delete the `@effect/platform` and `@effect/platform-node` dependencies and the whole `pnpm.packageExtensions` block (it only exists for them). Drop the `pnpm` key if it is left empty.
- In `knip.json`, delete the `@effect/platform` and `@effect/platform-node` entries of `ignoreDependencies`.
- In `packages/schemas/package.json`, set `dependencies.effect` to `^4.1.2`.
- Do not change `package.json`'s `scripts`.

Step 3: run `pnpm add effect@4.1.2` at the repository root. It writes `"effect": "^4.1.2"` and re-resolves `pnpm-lock.yaml`, which drops the platform packages.
Then read `pnpm-lock.yaml` and confirm three things: exactly one effect version (4.1.2) is resolved, no `@effect/platform`, `@effect/platform-node` or `@effect/platform-node-shared` entry remains, and both manifests say `^4.1.2`.
If the registry cannot be reached:
- stop at once, before the codemod;
- make the first line of the handoff say so;
- do not vendor the package and do not hand-edit `pnpm-lock.yaml`.
The operator then runs the same `pnpm add` in this worktree from outside the session and resumes. A gate that records counts on an Effect 3 tree must not be committed.

Step 5: compare the printed numbers with this phase's commit body. The body carries src before and after, tests before and after, and one rewrite count per rule, which the operator filled in before approval (q-commit-counts). If any number differs, stop and report both sets in the handoff; do not edit the body.

Step 6: record the real numbers in `docs/effect-4-mapping.md`. Its introduction says the counts that matter are the ones the first Effect 4 phase records.
- In §1, replace the Rewrites column and the trial-run sentence with this run's per-rule rewrites and files.
- State the four type-error counts.
- In §2, update the leftover totals per skill and the blocked-use table from this run's `left to phases` list.
- Keep the document's structure and its other text.

Step 7: refresh the history lock (§5.17).
- The codemod rewrote files under `src/schemas/history/`. For every such file whose bytes changed, recompute its entry in `packages/schemas/history.lock.json` as the sha256 hex of its bytes. Do this with a one-off `pnpm exec tsx` script that calls `sha256` from `packages/schemas/build/generated.ts`.
- Keep the keys sorted and the rendering of `renderLock` (two-space JSON plus a newline).
- Add no entry and remove none. `scripts/schemas-check.ts --write` cannot do this, because `refreshLock` never re-pins an existing entry, and it would also try to record snapshots. Do not run `--write`.

Step 8: run `pnpm codemod:effect4 --ratchet`. With no record at HEAD, it writes `scripts/effect4-codemod/type-error-counts.json` and `scripts/effect4-codemod/passing-tests.json` as the first record (§5.22). The phase's gate runs it again and records the same.
Never edit the paths the preamble lists as protected or read-only, the corpus case files, or `packages/schemas/snapshots/**`.
phases.boundaryContracts: Producer of the ratchet base for every later phase: `scripts/effect4-codemod/type-error-counts.json` (`{ src, tests }`) and `scripts/effect4-codemod/passing-tests.json`, both committed here and read at HEAD by the next gate. Producer of `packages/schemas/shipped-json.json` (file name to exact Effect 3 content), which phase-08's build and check consume as the byte reference of the shipped JSON Schemas.

commit.subject: build(deps): install effect 4.1.2 and apply the Effect 4 codemod
commit.body:
Move phax and @lbdremy/phax-schemas to effect ^4.1.2. Remove @effect/platform, @effect/platform-node and their packageExtensions. Apply the codemod's mechanical rewrites (pnpm codemod:effect4), then pnpm format.

Type errors (codemod run on the Effect 3 tree with effect 4.1.2 installed):
  src    <src-before> -> <src-after>
  tests  <tests-before> -> <tests-after>

Rewrites per rule:
  either-to-result      <n>
  effect-either         <n>
  schema-decode-either  <n>
  context-tag           <n>
  schema-filters        <n>
  schema-optional-with  <n>
  catch-all             <n>
  parse-result-issues   <n>

The codemod rewrote frozen decoders under src/schemas/history/. This commit refreshes packages/schemas/history.lock.json for them, as the Effect 4 migration's refresh.

The ratchet records the first type-error counts and the first set of passing tests. packages/schemas/shipped-json.json captures the JSON Schemas the package ships, rendered on Effect 3 before the install, as their byte reference.

phases.title: Schema topic: current schemas and the refusal adapter
phases.objective: The current schemas decode and refuse on Effect 4. phax's refusal model is built from Effect 4's issues by its one adapter, so every corpus refusal line can replay unchanged once its imports load. The schema symbols across src, tests, scripts and site are migrated, except the frozen decoders, the JSON Schema generator and the package.
detailedInstructions: Follows skill: effect4-schema (with effect4-lookup for every symbol). Read both skills, `docs/effect-4-mapping.md` §2 (effect4-schema table) and the topic guide `docs/vendor/effect-migration/effect@4.1.2/migration/schema.md` before editing.

`ParseResult.ParseError` is a blocker. After migrating it, re-run `pnpm exec tsx scripts/effect4-codemod/main.ts` so the covered uses it held back are rewritten mechanically, then run `pnpm format`. The codemod is deterministic per file, so this run leaves `src/schemas/history/**` unchanged; check that the history files' bytes did not move.

Read errors with `node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit`, and `-p tsconfig.test.json` for the tests. Run the corpus tests with `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run tests/unit/effect4Corpus tests/unit/schemas/refusal`. They may still fail at load on an Either the errors topic owns; record which ones and why. Never edit a corpus case, a baseline or a corpus test to make one pass.

Before finishing:
- run `pnpm codemod:effect4 --ratchet`: both counts at or below HEAD's, and every recorded test still passing;
- run the `--check` report: no `effect4-schema` leftover outside `src/schemas/history/`, `src/schemas/publishedJsonSchema.ts`, `packages/schemas/**` and the scripts/schemas-*.ts files.
If a count rose, continue migrating this topic's symbols where the new errors appeared; never silence them with `any` or `as`.
phases.boundaryContracts: The refusal model (`src/schemas/refusal/`) is the boundary between Effect and phax's words. Producer: `adapter.ts`, the one module that reads Effect's issues, which now come from SchemaIssue. Consumer: `render.ts` and every formatter, which read only the refusal value (path, kind, expected label, actual value). The shape of that value does not change. Consumers of the current schemas (app, cli, infra, the package) keep the same decoded types and refusal lines.

testStrategy.guarantee: every refused corpus input of config layers, documents, provider answers and current formats renders the captured refusal line, once its imports load
testStrategy.oracle: expected lines in tests/effect4Corpus/cases through replay.test.ts and wording.test.ts

testStrategy.guarantee: only src/schemas/refusal/adapter.ts reads Effect's issues, and no formatter in src matches Effect's message text

testStrategy.guarantee: the phase adds no any type, no silencing as assertion and no compatibility module
testStrategy.oracle: the phase's diff searched for any, as other than as const and fixture brands, and compat modules

testStrategy.guarantee: no expected value in any test moved
testStrategy.oracle: the phase's diff of tests/ restricted to expectation lines

testStrategy.guarantee: both type-error counts end at or below the previous phase's and every recorded test still passes
testStrategy.oracle: pnpm codemod:effect4 --ratchet against HEAD's records

src/schemas/publishedJsonSchema.ts, packages/schemas/** and scripts/schemas-*.ts (phase-08)

- The Effect 4 idioms chosen for the recurring patterns: pattern and length checks, filters with a jsonSchema annotation, optional keys, annotations, the SchemaIssue-to-refusal mapping. phase-03 reviews them and phase-04 and phase-08 repeat them.

commit.subject: refactor(schemas): migrate current schemas and the refusal adapter to Effect 4
commit.body:
Follow the effect4-schema skill for the current schemas: Schema filters and checks, optional keys, annotations, ParseError and the SchemaAST helpers, across src (outside the frozen decoders and the JSON Schema generator), tests, scripts and site.

src/schemas/refusal/adapter.ts now builds phax's refusal model from Effect 4's SchemaIssue. It is still the one module that reads Effect's issues, so no refusal line moves. tests/effect4Corpus/subjects.ts follows the migrated decoders. The codemod was re-run after the ParseError blocker.

phases.assignmentReason: This phase settles the Effect 4 Schema idiom no code in the repository shows yet, including the SchemaIssue-to-refusal mapping that every refusal line depends on. Two later phases repeat its pattern, so it takes claude-opus-5-5 at high.

phases.title: Review the Effect 4 schema pattern
phases.objective: A person reviews the Effect 4 schema idiom phase-02 set, and corrects it if needed, before phase-04 repeats it on the 63 frozen decoders and phase-08 on the package and the generator.
detailedInstructions: Follows skill: effect4-schema (with effect4-lookup for every symbol). This phase plans no file; the person's correction is committed by `phax resume` with the gate.

Review phase-02's diff and its handoff for these points:
- No `any`, no `as` standing in for a broken type (`as const` and fixture brands aside), no compatibility module, no API absent from the reference and the installed effect source (§5.11).
- The idioms chosen for `Schema.pattern`, the length and numeric checks, `Schema.filter` with a `jsonSchema` annotation, `optionalWith`, `.annotate(` and `Schema.SchemaError`. phase-04 copies them into the frozen decoders, whose bytes are locked, and phase-08 into the package formats and the generator.
- `src/schemas/refusal/adapter.ts`: each SchemaIssue kind maps to the refusal kind and label the Effect 3 adapter produced. No other module reads Effect's issues. No formatter reads message text.
- The corpus test status phase-02 reported, and whether any failure is phase-02's own rather than a later topic's.
- That no expected value in tests moved, and no protected, corpus or snapshot file changed.
A correction stays within the effect4-schema skill and the optional files below, or the files phase-02 already changed. It moves no refusal line.
implementationOrder: Read phase-02's handoff
Review the diff against the points above
Correct, then resume
excludedScope: Migrating the frozen decoders (phase-04) or the generator and package (phase-08)
Any symbol of the errors, services or core topics
phases.verification: The `effect-migration` gate profile in phax.json, run by `phax resume` on the person's correction.
phases.expectedHandoff: What the person changed, which idioms phase-04 and phase-08 must now follow, and any correction to the refusal adapter's mapping.

commit.subject: refactor(schemas): review corrections to the Effect 4 schema pattern
commit.body: A person reviewed the Effect 4 schema idiom and the refusal adapter that the schema topic set, before the frozen decoders and the package repeat them. Their corrections are committed here.

phases.title: Schema topic: the frozen decoders and the history lock
phases.objective: Every frozen decoder under src/schemas/history/ runs on Effect 4 and accepts and refuses exactly what it did on Effect 3, with the same decoded values and refusal lines. Its lock entries are re-pinned in this one commit, which names the Effect 4 migration.
detailedInstructions: Follows skill: effect4-schema (with effect4-lookup for every symbol). The skill's `May change` names `src/schemas/history/`. This phase migrates every v3 symbol under that path, of every topic (Schema, ParseResult, SchemaAST, and the `Either`, `Effect.catch*` or `Option` uses a decoder holds). Later codemod re-runs then find nothing there, and the lock is not refreshed a third time.

Repeat the idioms phase-02 set, as corrected at the phase-03 review (read both handoffs). Each frozen module is a self-contained released shape: change how it is written, never what it decodes. Do not merge two decoders, do not make one import a current schema it did not import, and do not add or remove a module (§5.18).

Migrate any blocker first, then re-run `pnpm exec tsx scripts/effect4-codemod/main.ts` so its covered uses are rewritten mechanically. `src/schemas/history` is excluded from oxfmt, so write it in the files' existing style.

Re-pin the lock (§5.17).

The existing tests in `tests/unit/schemasPackage/snapshots.test.ts` inject states with no documents and must keep passing unchanged: a text-equal pair is still equivalent, and a different pair with no documents is still a finding. - `shipped-json.json` itself does not change in this phase.

commit.subject: feat(schemas-package): ship Effect 4 schemas and judge JSON Schemas by the corpus
commit.body:
Port the JSON Schema generator and the package to Effect 4, following the effect4-schema skill. @lbdremy/phax-schemas exports Effect 4 Schema values under its 0.36.0 names, and its parse functions answer the corpus as before.

The schemas check now judges each format's generated JSON Schema against its latest released snapshot by the corpus documents both accept and refuse (ajv), not by text. An empty document list never proves equivalence. No next snapshot is recorded and no stamp moves. The package ships its JSON Schemas from packages/schemas/shipped-json.json, byte-identical to the Effect 3 rendering. docs/effect-4-mapping.md records what Effect 4's generator renders differently.

The tree passes check:full, the build, the site and the Deno smokes, and the codemod reports no v3 symbol.
